chunks: Are you not (residing) in the houses of those before you, who were of longer ages, better traces, had bigger desires, were more in numbers and had greater armies.

How they devoted themselves to the world and how they showed preference to it? Then they left it without any provision that could convey them through, or the back (of a beast for riding) to carry them.
Did you get the news that the world was ever generous enough to present ransom for them, or gave them any support or afforded them good company?

It rather inflicted them with troubles, made them languid with calamities, molested them with catastrophes, threw them down on their noses, trampled them under hoofs and helped the “vicissitudes of time” [52:30] against them.
ai.seo_question: How did previous generations devote themselves to the world and what was their ultimate fate according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from the Sermon of Caution, Imam Ali (AS) employs vivid rhetorical questions to dismantle the illusion of worldly permanence, contrasting the fleeting nature of previous generations' power and longevity with their sudden departure. He characterizes the world not as a loyal companion but as a burdensome entity that exhausts its devotees with calamities, thereby preparing them for the inevitable transition to the Hereafter. This reflection serves as a practical spiritual warning to prioritize eternal provisions over temporary worldly attachments.
